name: WCORR-PRIV-001: SSH access → privileged account creation
description: Detects a successful SSH login followed by sudo activity targeting root and a subsequent new-user event on the same monitored endpoint.
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=30m
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword == "5715" and
    data.dstuser.keyword != null
  ] by data.dstuser.keyword
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword in ("5402", "5407") and
    data.dstuser.keyword == "root" and
    data.srcuser.keyword != null and
    (
      data.command.keyword like "*useradd*" or
      data.command.keyword like "*adduser*"
    )
  ] by data.srcuser.keyword
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword == "5902"
  ] by ?data.srcuser.keyword
author: Wazuh EQL Correlation
false_positives: The source says the optional third-stage key accommodates missing data.srcuser and that account creation remains associated by agent and time. Optional-field syntax does not itself guarantee wildcard joining: missing values can become null and fail to join a non-null username. Verify this claim in the target engine; do not silently change the query. SSH-to-sudo attribution is stronger, but account creation causality remains unproven. sudo su followed by useradd in a root shell is intentionally excluded.
setup: Collect SSH destination usernames, sudo source usernames and commands, and 5902 new-user events. Validate stage-specific joins and missing third-stage usernames explicitly.
